papers.title: Hot Spots: From Smooth to Nonsmooth Simply Connected Planar Domains
papers.abstract: Assuming the absence of interior local extrema for first positive Neumann eigenfunctions on bounded smooth simply connected planar domains, as reported in \cite{SmoothInput}, we extend the hot spots conclusion to simply connected domains of finite area with compact Sobolev embedding and simple first positive Neumann eigenvalue. The supremum and infimum are approached in arbitrarily thin boundary layers. For bounded domains and eigenfunctions continuous up to the boundary, both extrema are attained on the boundary. We also transfer polynomial Neumann heat-kernel bounds uniformly along a conformal exhaustion and construct explicit bounded and unbounded examples, including domains with cusps and a domain with infinitely many corners and bottlenecks. Some of these examples admit no polynomial Neumann heat-kernel bound.

papers.title: Displacement structure and eigenvalue bounds for multiband prolate matrices
papers.abstract: We obtain explicit non-asymptotic bounds for the eigenvalue transition of multiband prolate matrices. Let $S\subset[-1/2,1/2]$ be a finite union of pairwise disjoint intervals, and let $\lambda_0\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_{N-1}$ be the eigenvalues of $B_{N,S}$. If $\nu$ is the number of boundary points of $S$ on the frequency torus, then, for every $0<\eps<1/2$, \[ \#\{k:\eps<\lambda_k<1-\eps\} \le \nu\ceil{\frac{\log(4N)}{\pi^2} \log\!\left(\frac{4}{\eps(1-\eps)}\right)}. \] Compared with the multiband estimate of Zhu and Wakin~\cite{wakin2017approximating}, this improves the dependence on $\eps$ from order $1/[\eps(1-\eps)]$ to logarithmic dependence. We also prove a second bound in which the main logarithmic term depends on the time--bandwidth product $N|S|$ rather than only on $N$. We also compare $S$ with frequency sets having fewer boundary points. Using a classical large-sieve estimate, we take into account not only the total size of the change in the frequency set, but also how that change is distributed. For sets with many small gaps, this can give a bound growing like $\log N$ for fixed $\eps$, even when the bounds based only on the total size of the gaps grow at least linearly in $N$. We also obtain exponential bounds for individual eigenvalues and use them to estimate the error in approximating sampled multiband signals by leading eigenvectors. A discretization argument gives corresponding results for the continuous problem. Numerical examples compare the bounds and examine how the locations of the frequency intervals affect the eigenvalues.

papers.title: Quantitative nodal domain count for Maass forms
papers.abstract: We consider a real even Hecke-Maass cusp form $\phi$ on the modular surface, with Laplace eigenvalue $1/4+T^2$. We prove that its restriction to any fixed compact segment $\beta$ of the vertical geodesic above $i$ has $\gg_{\beta,\varepsilon} T^{1/6-\varepsilon}$ sign changes, yielding the same lower bound for the number of distinct inert nodal domains meeting the segment. Building on ideas of Jang-Jung and Jung-Young, we study correlations between values at points on the vertical geodesic separated by distances of order $T^{-1}$. Using arithmetic quantum unique ergodicity and Dirichlet-polynomial estimates, we show that the correlation is negative for a suitable choice of separation. An elementary counting argument and the Iwaniec-Sarnak supremum bound then give the claimed lower bound.

papers.title: The Fixed-$q$ Edge Limit of the $q$-Krawtchouk Ensemble
papers.abstract: We study the fixed-$q$ right-edge asymptotics of the ordinary $q$-Krawtchouk ensemble. For $0<q<1$, finite polynomial duality gives a direct proof of convergence of the correlation kernels to an explicit limiting kernel. The local Jacobi limit is a shifted continuous $q^{-1}$-Hermite expression with an indeterminate moment problem, so the limiting Jacobi expression does not determine a unique self-adjoint operator. A single spectral atom, asymptotically saturating the mass bound, selects the realization and yields strong-resolvent convergence. The limiting kernel represents its positive spectral projection and admits spectral-series, Christoffel--Darboux, and partial-theta representations. After a ground-state transformation, the associated dual operator agrees with a two-step spatial Markov operator of Borodin--Corwin. For $q>1$, the limiting Jacobi operator is of Al-Salam--Carlitz~I type and is essentially self-adjoint.

papers.title: Optimization Inverse Spectral Problem for the Schr\"odinger Operator on a Compact Graph
papers.abstract: We study the optimization inverse spectral problem (OISP) for the first $m$ eigenvalues of the Schr\"odinger operator on a compact metric graph. We prove the existence of a solution for every strictly increasing finite set of prescribed eigenvalues. On a graph without cycles, we obtain a representation of the optimal correction as a linear combination of squared eigenfunctions, provided that the selected eigenvalues are simple and separated from the next eigenvalue. On a graph with cycles, under the same simplicity and separation assumptions, we obtain a strong limiting representation of the optimal potential in terms of eigenfunctions of approximating operators. For a graph with a cycle, we give a counterexample with simple eigenvalues and linearly dependent squared eigenfunctions. We also prove that linear dependence of the squares of nonzero restrictions to an edge of eigenfunctions corresponding to distinct eigenvalues forces the potential on that edge to have an analytic representative

papers.title: On the inequality $\mu_3 < \lambda_1$ for the eigenvalues of the Laplace operator
papers.abstract: In 1952, P\'olya proved the inequality $\mu_2 < \lambda_1$ for the eigenvalues of Dirichlet and Neumann problems in domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, $d \ge 2$. In 2026, Tang and Zhang proved the inequality $\mu_3 < \lambda_1$ in the two-dimensional case. We show that $\mu_3 < \lambda_1$ for $d\ge 3$ as well.
